seo.description: Art direction and photography for Ciele's Life Edition running collection.

projectCover.alt: Man wearing coat that floats in the wind — LE Collection by CIELE

projectPoster.alt: Man wearing coat that floats in the wind — LE Collection by CIELE

pageContent.title: Print. Scan. Repeat.
pageContent.text:
Halfway through cooking noodles in the back of a van, parked god-knows-where in Utah, Ciele called. They had a weird-in-the-best-way idea: a capsule built around jeans you could actually run in, and it needed visuals just as unexpected.

Back in Montreal, the sky was wet cement. No chance. So we stopped chasing weather and built our own world: studio lights, scanned textures, backgrounds torn up and rebuilt. Print, scan, print again

The result was less a campaign than its own dimension. Surreal but inviting, and tight enough to give the drop a clear identity. It ended up featured across several design-forward sport publications, and traveled further than we expected.

seo.title: 80 Winters — Auclair
seo.description: Celebrating 80 years of winter heritage with Auclair. Creative direction and video.

image.alt: Auclair 80 Winters ski film — backcountry skiing footage celebrating eight decades of Canadian winter craftsmanship

projectCover.alt: Auclair brand video showcasing outdoor winter gear and accessories in action

projectPoster.alt: Skier carving through deep powder in the Auclair 80 Winters film — celebrating 80 years of winter heritage

pageContent.title: Auclair turned 80. This wasn’t a regular seasonal push. It was about heritage.
pageContent.text: A brand that's been shaping gloves for generations. The twist? We had to shoot a winter concept in the middle of summer. So we stripped down a camera to run near-infrared, flipping green fields into stark white. We hauled in snow machines, built storms from nothing, and leaned into the surreal to make winter happen under the sun. Our director friend Rémi Belleville pushed the concept to its edge, pulling in a crew that thrived on the challenge. Every department leaned in: art, camera, sound each adding a layer that made the vision hit harder. The result walks a fine line: past, future and legacy. Timeless, but entirely its own.

seo.description: Trail running video series with Jay Du Temple for YouTube. Produced by Podium.

image.alt: Jay Du Temple trail running video — comedian and endurance athlete pushing limits on mountain trails

projectCover.alt: Jay Du Temple trail running video — comedian and endurance athlete pushing limits on mountain trails

projectPoster.alt: Jay Du Temple running on a mountain trail — trail running and YouTube video production project

pageContent.title: A docu series that launched Jay’s YouTube Channel.
pageContent.text:
In the Alps, mid-shoot, Phil’s watch lit up. Jay Du Temple, out of the blue. He wanted to document his build to his longest race yet, a 125 km. They didn’t know each other, but Jay’s tone felt grounded, open.

Phil met him in Kenya. Jay was cruising, tossing jokes mid-stride. Then it was back home for the long hauls: 160 km traverses, night starts, and the unglamorous middle. Jay was breaking personal limits. Phil was breaking tripods.

It became a four-part series that launched Jay’s YouTube: an honest look at what it means to start a sports series, and actually go all in.

pageContent.title: Over 600k views on YouTube, the project really connected with viewers.

seo.title: Not Quite Gone — Le Braquet Cycling Club
seo.description: Cycling film for Le Braquet Cycling Club. Creative direction and video by Podium.

image.alt: Man wearing coat that floats in the wind — LE Collection by CIELE

pageContent.title: We built a 2-meter high wheel totem and transported it by canoe as the tide rose around us.
pageContent.text: We wanted to break the expected utility of the wheel by treating it not as a literal object that helps you move faster, but as a burden carried against its intended purpose. Entirely shot on 16mm with a desynced shutter and no monitor, we built a 3-meter high wheel totem and transported it by canoe as the tide rose around us.

pageContent.title: Red earth, New ground
pageContent.text: As Kenyans slowly step into the world of trail running, we had the chance to meet the ones leading the way: the Milimani Runners. We built the project in two parts. First, in Kenya, observing their daily rhythm and capturing their workouts. Then, in studio, creating a more abstract space, where red earth meets shadows, sweat, and textures. Salomon gave us full trust. Just, "make something interesting." That kind of freedom doesn't happen often. And it made all the difference.

pageContent.title: The brief was simple: capture what summer feels like in Montreal
pageContent.text: By a warm April day we met with Dan, Marketing Director at Ciele. He and his friend Drew Tyndell, a mixed-media artist from New York, were prepping a campaign. The brief was simple: capture what summer feels like in Montreal and make it pulse with life. From that idea we built surreal dimensions that run through underground tunnels and familiar streets. We even covered a pool with black tarp so we could shoot underwater, using light to create surreal effects.

seo.title: Western States — Salomon
seo.description: Trail running documentary for Salomon at Western States. Creative direction and video.

image.alt: Salomon Western States 100 ultramarathon film — endurance runners conquering Sierra Nevada mountain trails

projectPoster.alt: Ultra runner on the Western States 100 trail through Sierra Nevada mountains — Salomon endurance film poster

pageContent.title: Western States isn't just another 100-miler.
pageContent.text:
It started with horses, then one guy decided to run it. The rest is trail-running legend.

Salomon asked for something different for this recap. Not the usual hero montage. We linked with Quanine Studio in France and bent the footage in ways the ultra-trail world hadn't seen. On the ground we chased the grit and the weird beauty of a race that never gets easier. The climbs, the falls, the middle-of-the-night silence.

Shot through old lenses. The frames carry weight. So does the story.
